tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

classiq-page-scope-no-results: Whole page read (about 3 KB): it is an overview that closes by listing Getting Started, Constraints, Preferences. No experiment, number, theorem or proof appears. The AI-assistant notice is in the text layer as quoted.
t1-t2-definitions: Coherence times section, p.3: the article defines the relaxation rate (T1) and the coherence time (T2) in these words.
clops-definition: CLOPS section, p.6: CLOPS is defined as relying on QV and measuring how many QV circuits a QPU runs per unit of time, as the runtime-interaction metric.
article-scope-and-nature: Introduction, p.2: the article states the topics it highlights (hardware and qubit characterization, gate-level errors, certification via algorithms) and refers readers to a more detailed report on request.
cyc-canonicalization-objectives: Page 1, 'Canonicalization Objectives': the page lists objectives (a) compression, (b) correctness, (c) speed, each defined as quoted.
cyc-commutative-argument-ordering: Page 1, after the five-formula example: states that a single HL construct involves canonicalizing argument order for a commutative relation, here #$and. Design of its own component.
cyc-no-completeness-guarantee: Page 1: the page states that the canonicalizer cannot guarantee mapping all equivalent EL formulae to one HL construct, since FOL is undecidable. The soundness and speed guarantees in the value are vendor assertions with no proof, but the limit is the core statement.
cyc-commutativity-index-responsibility: Page 1, implementation note: states the design consequence for the inference engine and KB indexing. Design of its own system, as stated.
cyc-canonicalizer-components: Page 1: the page defines the four components (a) critic, (b) pre-processor, (c) translator, (d) post-processor with their roles, as quoted.
cyc-critic-checks: Page 1, critic paragraph: syntax by BNF parse, semantics by arity and argument constraints; the canonicalization outcomes for ill-formed formulae are stated as quoted. Specification of its own component.
cyc-arity-declarations: Page 1: fixed and variable arity are defined, with #$and and #$different as variable-arity examples, and the critic's arity requirement is stated.
cyc-typed-relations-microtheory-specific: Page 1: typing constraints per argument, function result types, microtheory-specific declarations and the arg-type check are stated as quoted.
cyc-canonicalization-microtheory-relativ: Page 1, implementation note: canonicalization is relative to a designated microtheory and may differ between microtheories. States the scope of the component's behavior.
cyc-exceptions-to-abnormal: Page 1, pre-processor paragraph: #$ExceptWhen and #$ExceptFor become #$abnormal assertions, and the meaning of #$ExceptWhen is stated as quoted.
cyc-exceptwhen-translation-form: Page 1: the transformed form and the meaning of <variables> and <kb-assertion> are stated as quoted.
cyc-translator-clause-output: Page 1, translator paragraph: after the six listed steps the page states they produce one or more clauses per well-formed EL formula. A trivial but accurate description of its own algorithm.
cyc-rule-macros-definition: Page 1, post-processor paragraph: the page defines a rule macro and states that special inference modules typically support each, with the #$genls example.
cyc-postprocessor-component-canonicaliza: Page 1, end of the post-processor paragraph: the three steps (ordering commutative arguments with the two techniques, reifying function terms, replacing EL with HL variables) are listed as quoted.
cyc-deduction-not-sound: Section 6, p.14: the authors state that deduction is sound in general, but that because nearly all of Cyc's KB is default-true, deduction in Cyc is not sound, and that Cyc should give multiple answers with pro and con arguments. A stated limit of their own system.
darji2024-scope-unknown-centroid-brightn: Abstract, p.1: states what the classifier is tested on (one source versus two sources well within the Rayleigh limit, no prior knowledge of centroid or brightness). The experiment on pp.2-4 matches.
darji2024-hypothesis-cases-a-b: p.2: cases A and B are defined, with density matrices in Eqs. 1 and 2.
darji2024-projection-modes-gaussian-and-: p.2: the first projection mode is the Gaussian (0th order HG) mode, and the second is a superposition of 30 HG modes. Its own method as built.
darji2024-pump-mode-hg-indices: p.2, before the optimization paragraph: the superposition mode consists of 30 HGmn modes with m=1,3,5,7,9 and n=0..5, as stated.
darji2024-extinction-ratio-test: p.2: Rj=Oj/Gj, threshold Rt in Eq. 3 with shot-noise terms, and the classification rule (below Rt gives case A, else case B), all defined as stated.
darji2024-classification-fidelity-defini: p.2, Eq. 4: C = 1/2[P(A|A)+P(B|B)], with P(j|k) the probability of classifying case k as case j.
darji2024-error-probability-complement: p.3 (paragraph after Fig. 3): the parenthetical states that error probability is the complement of the fidelity defined here. Stated as the relation between the two.
darji2024-experiment-laser-wavelengths: p.2, experimental setup paragraph: 50 MHz mode-locked laser, 1558.53 nm pump, 1545.32 nm signal, 775.948 nm up-converted light, as quoted.
darji2024-experiment-ppln-detector: p.2, setup paragraph: PPLN crystal (HC Photonics, 50x12.3x1 mm) at the Fourier plane, beam FWHM about 120 um, Si-APD ID100 with dark counts about 2 Hz.
darji2024-experiment-slm-signal-displace: p.2, setup paragraph: pump in an optimized superposition of 30 HG modes; signal SLM uses blaze grating masks to displace the signal on the horizontal axis.
darji2024-optimization-simulation-presel: pp.2-3: split-step simulation of SFG picks 30 modes from 300 random modes, because direct testing is limited by SLM speed. Procedure as stated.
darji2024-optimization-pso-in-experiment: p.3: the 30 simulated modes seed a particle swarm optimization run in the experiment, 20 iterations per run, convergence set to maximize RB-RA, velocity weights reduced tenfold every third iteration.
darji2024-fig3-test-design: p.3, text and Fig. 3 caption: four separations 0.2 to 0.8 sigma, misalignment up to the separation, equal strength (epsilon=0.5), about 500 and 5000 photons.
darji2024-fig3-error-bars: p.3, Fig. 3 caption: error bars are 95% confidence intervals from 10 runs with 1000 data points each.
darji2024-fig4-test-design: pp.3-4, text and Fig. 4 caption: four brightness values epsilon in [0.5,0.8], no misalignment, about 750 photons, 10 runs of 100 data points, 95% confidence intervals.
darji2024-limit-narrow-signal-band: p.4: the authors state that for a given pump wavelength the current setup is efficient only for a narrow signal band. The broadband remark is a suggestion, not a result.
